Sorted list of 84 distinct triangle areas corresponding to the unique solution to the problem of placing 9 points on a grid rectangle of minimal area, such that all triangles formed by any 3 of the points have distinct areas > 0.
Smallest number that can be obtained from the "Choix de Bruxelles", version 2 (A323460) operation applied to n.
The order of square grid cells touched by a circle expanding from the middle of a cell read by antidiagonals.
Integers which are the sum of distinct primes of the form 6*n - 1.
Number of strict integer partitions of n containing no prime indices of the parts.
Number of integer partitions of n containing no prime indices of the parts.
a(n) = the smallest number k such that floor(sigma(k)/tau(k)) = n, or 0 if no such number k exists.
Heinz numbers of integer partitions of powers of 2.
"Sloping quaternary numbers": write numbers in quaternary under each other (right-justified), read diagonals in upward direction, convert to decimal.
Number of separable partitions of n in which the number of distinct (repeatable) parts is 2.
Triangle read by rows giving the number of configurations of n indistinguishable pairs placed on the vertices of the ladder graph P_2 X P_n such that exactly k such pairs are joined by an edge.
Number of partitions of n into 9 squarefree parts.
Values of A326764 along the Y-axis.

Numbers k that are not prime powers (i.e., not in A000961) such that A328925(k) > 1; numbers k such that if we write k = Product_{i=1..t} p_i^e_i , then t > 1, and lcm_{1<=i,j<=t, i!=j} ord(p_i,p_j^e_j) < A002322(k), where ord(a,r) is the multiplicative order of a modulo r, and A002322 is the Carmichael lambda (usually written as psi).
For every n >= 0, exactly seven sums are prime among a(n+i) + a(n+j), 0 <= i < j < 7; lexicographically earliest such sequence of distinct nonnegative numbers.
For every n >= 0, exactly nine sums are prime among a(n+i) + a(n+j), 0 <= i < j < 7; lexicographically earliest such sequence of distinct nonnegative numbers.
Numbers having twice as many 1's in their binary expansion as terms in their Zeckendorf expansion.
a(n) = n + floor(ns/r) + floor(nt/r), where r = Pi - 1, s = Pi, t = Pi + 1.
a(n) = n + floor(n*s/r) + floor(n*t/r), where r = phi - 1/2, s = phi, t = phi + 1/2, and phi is the golden ratio = (1+sqrt(5))/2.
Plain Bob Infinity. Select terms <= n to get a permutation whose powers generate all possible pairs of bells for change ringing.
a(n) = n - A309639(n), where A309639(n) is the index of the least harmonic number H_i whose denominator (A002805) is divisible by n.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms that can be viewed as an irregular table where the n-th row has A000005(a(n)) terms and T(n, k) is a multiple of the k-th divisor of a(n) (=A027750(a(n), k)).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms that can be viewed as an irregular table where the n-th row has a(n) terms and for n > 1, T(n, k) is a multiple of k.
Least m > n such that 2^m - 2^n + 1 is prime.
a(n) is the greatest divisor v of A331220(n) such that the ternary representations of v and of A331220(n)/v have the same number of digits d for d = 0..2.
a(n) is the least divisor u of A331221(n) such that the decimal representations of u and of A331221(n)/u have the same number of digits d for d = 0..9.
Savannah problem: number of distinct possible populations after n weeks, allowing populations after the empty set.
Number of strict integer partitions of n whose first differences (assuming the last part is zero) are unimodal.
Starting from sigma(n), number of tripling steps to reach 1 in '3x+1' problem, or -1 if 1 is never reached.
Starting from sigma(n)+1, number of tripling steps to reach 1 in '3x+1' problem, or -1 if 1 is never reached.
Number of isomorphism classes which minimize the Wiener index among all 4-connected triangulations.
Sort all positive integers, first by sum of prime indices (A056239), then by number of prime indices (A001222).
Sort all positive integers, first by sum of prime indices (A056239), then by decreasing number of prime indices (A001222).
The sum of the Hamming weights of the elements of the Collatz orbit of n.
a(n) is the number of partitions of n of the form [k,k,b(1),b(2),...], where k>=b(1)>b(2)>...>=2.
Heinz numbers of all integer partitions sorted first by sum, then by length, and finally reverse-lexicographically.
Permutation of nonnegative integers that converts A162912 into A162911.
Squarefree numbers m such that the equation x*(x+1)*(x+2) = m*y^2 has at least one solution (x,y) with x > 0 and y > 0.
The cardinalities of the sets A(n), where A(0) is the empty set and A(n+1) is the union of A(n) and the Collatz orbit of the smallest natural number missing in A(n).
a(n) = floor(n/10) + (5 times last digit of n).
Numbers having at least one 4 in their representation in base 5.
Coordination sequence for Even Conant Lattice with respect to origin.
Number of distinct positive integer pairs, (s,t), such that s < t < n where neither s nor t divides n, and (s + t) | (s * t).
Nonpositive values in A117966, in order of appearance and negated.
Squares visited by either knight when a white knight and a black knight are moving on a spirally numbered board, always to the lowest available unvisited square; white moves first.
a(n) = L(L(n)) mod n, where L = Lucas numbers = A000032.
Irregular triangle read by rows where row n lists all semiprimes whose prime indices sum to n.
Irregular triangle read by rows where row n lists all squarefree semiprimes with prime indices summing to n.
Semiprimes whose prime indices sum to an even number.
Squarefree semiprimes whose prime indices sum to an even number.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of unoriented series-parallel networks whose multigraph has n edges and k interior vertices, 0 <= k < n.
Numbers k such that A318996(k) is prime.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier that shares a digit but not a factor > 1 with a(n-1).
Number of integer partitions of n with strictly decreasing first quotients.
Frobenius number of the odious numbers (A000069) starting with the n-th term.
Numbers k such that A340180(k) is prime.
Positions in A341334 of words in which #0's - #1's is odd.
Surface area of a right prism whose base is a regular n-gon with unit side length and unit height (rounded to the nearest integer).
Lexicographically earliest sequence S of distinct positive terms such that the sum of the last k digits of S is odd, k being the rightmost digit of a(n).
Numbers whose square can be represented in exactly one way as the sum of a square and a biquadrate (fourth power).
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (row k of A066099) has reverse-alternating sum < 0.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (row k of A066099) has reverse-alternating sum -2.
There are a(n) digits between a(n) and the next copy of the string a(n). This is the lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms with this property.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the first digit of a(n) is visible in a(n) * a(n+1).
Numbers k such that the numerator of the fractional part of the k-th harmonic is a prime number.
a(n) is the number of squares k^2 with n^2 <= k^2 <= n^3.
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive integers such that for any four consecutive terms a,b,c,d, d is prime to a and c, but not to b.
a(n) is the maximum number of key comparisons required to sort n records with distinct keys using a modified heapsort (Algorithm H in Don Knuth's TAOCP Vol. 3, answer to exercise 18).
Positive integers k such that if p is the next prime > k, and q is the previous prime < k, then p - k is prime and k - q is prime.
Number of partitions of n such that 5*(smallest part) = (number of parts).

Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the minimum number of alphabetic symbols in a regular expression for the k lexicographically first palindromes of odd length 2*n-1 over a binary alphabet, n >= 1, 1 <= k <= 2^n.
a(1) = 1, for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that is a multiple of the smallest prime that does not divide a(n-1).
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive numbers such that, for n>2, a(n) has a common factor with the second largest previous term but not with the largest previous term.
Number of strict integer partitions of n with same number of even parts as odd conjugate parts.
a(1) = 1. For n >= 2, a(n) is the least nonprime not already in the sequence such that there is at least one prime between a(n-1) and a(n).

Irregular table read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of regions formed after k diagonals, with k>=0, are drawn between vertices of a regular n-gon, with n>=3, when each vertex is fully connected to all other vertices in counterclockwise order before the next vertex, in counterclockwise order, is chosen.
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that is coprime to a(n-1) but does not equal a(n-1)+1.
Conjecturally the number of positive even integers that can be expressed as the sum of two distinct primes in exactly n ways.
a(n) is the least k > n such that A109812(n) AND A109812(k) = A109812(n) (where AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).

Irregular table read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of regions formed after k diagonals, with k>=0, are drawn between vertices of a regular n-gon, with n>=3, when each vertex in turn is connected to the vertex two to its left, then three to its left, then four... until all vertices are connected by diagonals.
Polynomials over GF(2) that are divisible by (x+1)^2 = x^2+1, encoded as binary numbers.

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive integers such that in any run of four consecutive terms there is only one pair of terms which share a prime divisor, the rest are all pairwise coprime.
Positions of nonzero terms in A354883.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the number of terms in the first n-1 terms of the sequence that share a 1-bit with n in their binary expansions.

a(n) is the number at the apex of a triangle whose base contains the distinct powers of 2 summing to n (in ascending order), and each number in a higher row is the bitwise XOR of the two numbers directly below it; a(0) = 0.
Numbers k such that the sum of (q mod p) for pairs of primes p<q such that p+q=2*k is prime.
Numbers k such that 5^k and 8^k have the same leading digit.
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest positive number not occurring earlier such that a(n) is coprime to the previous Omega(a(n-1)) terms.
Number of partitions of n into at most 4 distinct nonprime parts.
Sum of the number of divisors of floor(n/(b*c)) with b,c > 0 and b*c <= n.
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; thereafter let p be the smallest prime that does not divide a(n-2)*a(n-1), then a(n) is the smallest multiple of p that is not yet in the sequence.
Number of pairs of positive integers (k,i) such that k >= i and there exists an integer partition of n of length k with i distinct parts.

a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest positive number which has not appeared that shares a factor with a(n-2) + a(n-1) while the sum a(n) + a(n-1) is distinct from all previous sums a(i) + a(i-1), i=2..n-1.
Number of partitions of n whose least part is a multiple of 5.
a(n) is the length of the initial transient, before the periodic part, on the n-th diagonal from the left of rule-30 1-D cellular automaton, when started from a single ON cell.
Expansion of Sum_{k>0} k * x^k / (1 - x^(3*k-1)).
Sum of divisors of 5*n-1 of form 5*k+4.
Number of strict integer partitions of n with a part equal to the sum of two distinct others. A variation of sum-full strict partitions.

Let x, y  be the greatest exponents of 2, 3 respectively such that 2^x, 3^y do not exceed n and let k_2, k_3 be n - 2^x, and n - 3^y respectively. Then for n such that k_2 = 0 or k_3 = 0, a(n) = n, else a(n) is the least novel number Min{p*a(k_2), q*a(k_3)}, where p, q are primes not equal to either 2 or 3.
Triangle read by rows where T(n,k) is the number of integer partitions of n that can be linearly combined with nonnegative coefficients to obtain k.
3-valuation r(n) of the terms A367083(A367084(n)+1) = 3^r(n) which are the odd terms preceded by another odd term.
Semiprimes p*q such that 2*p divides q-1.
The slowest increasing sequence of semiprimes such that a(n-1) + a(n) is prime.
Table T(n, k) read by downward antidiagonals: T(n, k) = floor((4*T(n, k-1)+3)/3) starting with T(n, 0) = 4*n.
Triangular array T, read by rows: T(n,k) = number of sums |x-y|+|y-z| = k, where x,y,z are in {1,2,...,n} and x < y and y > z.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the lexicographically first Erdős sequence for the n-cycle graph having smallest possible maximum value.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that for any n > 0, a(n+1), a(2*n+1) and a(2*n+2) have a common prime factor.

a(1) = 1. Thereafter, if A007947(a(n-1)) is a term in A002110, a(n) is the smallest prime not already in the sequence. Otherwise a(n) is the smallest novel multiple of p, the greatest prime < g = gpf(a(n-1)).
Number of partitions of n into distinct parts such that number of parts is a multiples of 4.
Number of distinct partitions p of n such that max(p) == 1 mod 3.
Number of partitions of n such that (smallest part) >= 2*(number of parts).
Number of k in the range s(1), ..., s(n-1) such that gcd(k, s(n)) > 1, where s = A089088.
For n>=4, irregular triangular array of successive integer solutions to sqrt((d-c)*b^2 + c*(b+1)^2) for square integers d = n^2, where b and c are positive integers and c < d, read by rows.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest unused positive number such that a(n) is coprime to a(n-1) and (a(n) AND a(n-1)) = min(a(n), a(n-1)), where AND is the binary AND operation.
a(n) is the least k such that A001615(k) = 2*n, or -1 if there is no such k, where A001615 is the Dedekind psi function.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,m) is the number of unlabeled graphs with n vertices having m minimum forbidden subgraphs, n >= 1, 1 <= m <= A371162(n).

a(1) = 1. Thereafter, if A007947(a(n-1)) is in A002110, a(n) = smallest prime not already a term (condition [A]). Otherwise, if q is the greatest prime < Gpf(a(n-1)) which does not divide a(n-1), a(n) is the least novel multiple of q,(condition [B]).

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive integers such that any term j = a(n-1) with primorial kernel is followed by a prime, whereas any other term is followed by a number with prime factors p < q = Gpf(j) which do not divide j.
Nonnegative integers k such that either k = 0 or there is a perfect power x in the range prime(k) < x < prime(k+1).
Numbers k such that there is a unique perfect-power x in the range prime(k) < x < prime(k+1).
Square array read by upward antidiagonals: T(n,k) = ((k + n - 1)^2 + (k - n + 1)*(-1)^n + (1 - k - n)*(-1)^k + (1 - k - n)*(-1)^(k + n) + 2)/2.
Number of subgroups of S_n isomorphic to S_3 up to conjugacy, where S_n is the n-th symmetric group.
a(1) = 1. For n > 1 if a(n-1) is a novel term a(n) = number of a(i); 1 <= i <= n-1 whose sum of decimal digits does not exceed A007953(a(n-1)). If a(n-1) has occurred k (>1) times, a(n) = k*a(n-1).
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest unused positive number that is either coprime to both a(n-1) and a(n-2) or shares a factor with both a(n-1) and a(n-2).
a(1) = 1. For n > 1, a(n) is the earliest novel squarefree number divisible by the smallest prime which does not divide a(n-1).
a(n) = n + sum of prime indices of n.
Composite terms in A381019 in order of appearance.
Semiprimes k such that 6*k + 1 is also a semiprime.
MM-numbers of sets of sets with distinct sums.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that the product of two consecutive terms is always a triangular number (A000217).

a(2n) and a(2n+1) are the square spiral numbers of the position on which the (n+1)th domino is placed, when tiling the plane by placing the dominos always as near as possible to the origin and so that no two dominos share a long side. Inverse permutation of A383191.
Index of -n in A377090, or -1 if -n does not appear there.
The number of integers k from 1 to n such that the greatest divisor of k that is a unitary divisor of n is a 5-rough number (A007310).
Decreasing partition array based on the sequence (sin(n)); see Comments.

Triangle read by rows, based on Fibonacci numbers: Let i > 1 be such that F(i) <= n < F(i+1); i.e., i = A130233(n). Then T(n, k) = F(i-1)^2 + 1 - (i-1) mod 2 + (n - F(i)) * F(i-2) + (k-1) * F(i-1) where F(k) = A000045(k).

a(1) = 1, a(2) = 3; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest unused positive number that differs from a(n-1) by more than 1 and shares a factor with a(n-1) if a(n-1) < a(n-2), else it is coprime to a(n-1) if a(n-1) > a(n-2).

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive numbers such that, for n > 2, a(n) shares a factor with a(n-1) and is coprime to a(n-2) if a(n-1) > a(n-2), else it is coprime to a(n-1) and shares a factor with a(n-2) if a(n-1) < a(n-2).

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive numbers such that, for n > 2, a(n) shares a factor with a(n-1) and is coprime to a(n-2) if a(n-1) < a(n-2), else it is coprime to a(n-1) and shares a factor with a(n-2) if a(n-1) > a(n-2).. Start with a(1) = 1, a(2) = 4, a(3) = 9.
The binary expansion of the n-th term of A074832, when read backwards, corresponds to that of the a(n)-th term of A074832.
Position of the even Markoff numbers 2*A388289 in A002559.
Number computed by Wolfram's 3-state 2-symbol Turing machine 1342057 when started with n on the tape.
Upper (1/4)-midsequence of square numbers and (-1)*(triangular numbers); see Comments.
a(n) is the smallest index k such that A390084(k) = n.
Numbers k not in A000961 such that A001414(k) is in A000961.
The values of A390868(k) when k runs over the integers that are not exponentially odd.

When constructing the sequence of the positive integers > 1 from prime factors, we reuse the prime factors of the smallest earlier constructed numbers where we can. The sequence is the numbers whose prime factors were first reused entirely in the process.
a(n) is the number of twin prime pairs entirely within the sets of length prime(n) that are incrementally taken from the sequence of odd consecutive primes.
Guaranteed win if opponent chooses one of three baskets and the player chooses the coins with values from 1 to n (see Comments for details).

a(n) is the value of A280500(n*k, k) for the smallest odd k > 1 for which this value is not zero, where A280500 implements the carryless base-2 division, and returns 0 if the division leaves nonzero remainder.
Number of automorphism group orders that occur for exactly one unlabeled tree with n vertices.

Consider the first quadrant with its squares numbered by the square spiral, with initial square numbered 0, as in A392181. A knight starts at square 0 and always moves to the lowest-numbered square it has not visited. Sequence gives its trajectory (which is finite).
Positive integers expressible as a difference of two nonzero rational fourth powers.
Positive integers expressible as a difference of two rational fourth powers.
a(n) is the greatest k < n such that {phi*k} < {phi*n}, where {} denotes the fractional part and phi = A001622.
Length of row n in the irregular triangle A397173.
The canonical snowball representation of A398153(n), when read backwards, corresponds to that of A398153(a(n)).
a(n) is the number of die sizes < n that can produce n as the product of two identical dice.
a(0) = 0; a(1) = 1; thereafter a(n) = a(n-1) - 1 if that is not already in the sequence, otherwise a(n) = a(n-1) + floor(sqrt(a(n-1))).
Number of partitions of n where the smallest part is equal to the number of divisors of n, d(n) = A000005(n).
7030: Records in A245203 (= least k>=0 such that 4n+3 is the mean of primes 4(n-k)+3 and 4(n+k)+3).

Primes p such that the congruence 2^x == 3 (mod p) is solvable.
Prime determinants of forms with class number 2.
Primes for which -10 is a primitive root.
Primes p which divide no f(q)-1 or f(q)+1 for prime q < p, where f(q) is the product of all primes <= q.
Smallest nonempty set S containing prime divisors of 8k+7 for each k in S.
Primes p such that 29 is a square mod p.
Primes p such that 46 is not a square mod p.
Primes p such that 86 is a square mod p.
Primes p such that 97 is not a square mod p.
Primes p such that x^3 = 5 has a solution mod p.
Primes p such that p + 2 is squarefree.

Primes which are the sum of a prime number of consecutive primes.
Primes expressible as the sum of (at least two) consecutive primes in at least 1 way.
a(1) = 2; a(n+1) is the smallest prime not already in the sequence which differs from a(n) at every digit.
Numbers k such that there is no x < k such that sigma(x) = phi(k).
Numbers n such that 210*n -/+ 13 are primes.
Primes such that iterated sum-of-digits (A038194) is even.
Primes of the form x^2 + y^2 + 3 (x,y nonnegative).
Binary emirps, primes whose binary reversal is a different prime.
Concatenation of prime k and its 10's complement is a prime.
Decimal primes whose decimal representation in base 16 is also prime.
Primes that remain prime when their leading digit in binary representation is replaced by 0.
Length of repunits of which the prime factor-digit-excess computed by A095414 equals 0.
a(n) is the least prime greater than a(n-1) such that n is a quadratic residue mod p.
Half-period primes, i.e., primes p for which the decimal expansion of 1/p has period (p-1)/2.
Decimal primes whose decimal representation in hex is also prime.
Prime numbers n for which the square excess of the n-th prime is prime.
Primes of the form 2x^2+2xy+7y^2, with x and y nonnegative.
Primes of the form 2x^2-2xy+7y^2, with x and y nonnegative.
a(n) = smallest prime such that a(n) + 2n is also prime and such that a(n) > a(n-1).
Chen primes: primes p such that p + 2 is either a prime or a semiprime.
Chen primes that are not Fibonacci numbers.
Primes prime(n) such that there exists a 0 < k < n-1 such that prime(n+k) + prime(n-k) = 2*prime(n).
Primes p such that p+q+r, where p, q, r are consecutive primes, equals s+t+1, where s and t are consecutive primes.
Primes whose integer square root remainder is also prime.
Primes in A139252 (related to the toothpick structure).
Primes p such that p + 10 is not a prime.
a(n) = smallest member of the n-th term in S(3) (defined in Comments).
Primes p such that ratio in A154754 is 1.
Primes which are not in A173970 or A173971.
Prime numbers p such that p-LargestCube is prime, (LargestCube <= p).
Prime numbers p such that p-LargestSquare is prime and p-LargestCube is also prime, (LargestSquare <= p, LargestCube <= p).
Primes such that p(i)+p(i+1)+p(i+2) is a prime when all addends are taken modulo 10.
Primes p such that the minimum value of |p-2^x|, x>0, is also a prime.
Fixed points of a sequence h(n) defined by the minimum number of 3's in the relation n*[n,3,3,...,3,n] = [x,...,x] between simple continued fractions.
Primes p such that p mod 16 < 8.
Primes which cannot be written in the form a^2 + 6*b^2.
Numbers not divisible by 2, 3 or any prime of the form 4x^2+2xy+7y^2 (see A219908).
Least prime, q, greater than the previous prime, p, which is a primitive root of p; beginning with 2.
Least prime p such that the concatenation of primes from prime(n) to p is prime.
Chen primes p such that there are Chen primes p > q > r in arithmetic progression.
Numbers n such that A256832(n)/A000129(n-1) is not divisible by n.
Primes p such that every suffix of the binary representation of p is either a prime or 1.
Primes p such that every suffix of the base-4 representation of p is a prime.
Primes p such that L(p^2) = (p-1)*L(p)/2, where L(i) = A279186(i).
Primes p such that every suffix of the base-4 representation of p is either a prime or 1.
Primes p such that p does not divide any term of the Apery-like sequence A002895.
Primes p such that p does not divide any term of the Apery-like sequence A290576.
Rational primes that decompose in the field Q(sqrt(-13)).
Primes p such that Legendre(-13,p) = 0 or 1.
Primes p for which the continued fraction expansion of sqrt(p) does not have a 1 in the second position.
Primes p with 2 zeros in a fundamental period of A006190 mod p.
Primes such that p + digitsum(p, base 8) is again a prime.

Initial terms are the first 11 odd prime numbers. After that each new term in the sequence is the sum of whichever subset of the previous 11 terms gives the smallest prime number that is larger than the largest term so far.
The Judd Trump's "infinite plant" sequence: prime numbers become nonprime numbers by striking the cue ball 2 with a cue stick to the right (see the Comments section).
Integers k such that Z[sqrt(k)] = Z[x]/(x^2 - k) is a unique factorization domain.
Integers that cannot be expressed as x + y + z + x*y*z for x,y,z >= 1.
a(n) is the number of distinct lengths between consecutive points of the Farey sequence of order n.
Primes of the form p^2 + 2*q, where p and q are primes.
Primes in A161601 whose binary reversal is prime.
7032: If k appears so do 2k-2 and 3k-3. (duplicates omitted.)
First differences give digits of Pi = 3.1415926...
